title: Choplifter
build: Broderbund's original 1982 disk: Choplifter.woz (SHA-1 1c498365...41efc94) from archive.org's A Woz A Day collection, item wozaday_Choplifter, run on an Apple II Plus; analysed at the loader's hand-over to $0800 (orientation.md)

credits.role: the game's author (the title screen; the disk's WOZ metadata)

tools.emulator: Apple2TS 3.7.0 (git c900979), bundled by the kit into its server (kit/apple2), as an Apple II Plus (--model iiplus); check-emulator 49 passed, 0 failed, on 20 October 2026
tools.disassembler: regenerator2000 0.9.20 in its Apple II mode, driven through kit/apple2/r2000.py
tools.host: Linux 6.18 x86_64, Ubuntu 24.04, a hosted cloud session with no display

accuracy.note: 60 of the 835 comments written by hand and 20 of the 202 a script wrote on the shapes; the 13 wrong were all by hand, corrected with the 37 comments that said the same

the sound effects and the attract mode, run from the listing and held to Apple2TS click for click and frame for frame, and the tank slip, run from the listing against the page's model; building the sound player found the noise routine's two comments calling it an explosion's, when a tank or a jet firing is all that calls it; drawing the helicopter at each tilt from the listing, held to Apple2TS byte for byte, found the comments on land_height_table ($7895) and heli_height ($0006) saying a tilted helicopter lands higher, when the heights only keep a skid on the ground

exclude: the loader's stages, over the input buffer, page 3 and text page 1: the boot code that reads the disk, checks the Monitor ROM and sums the game (orientation.md, "The loader"). Its error printer at $0320 stays in memory as the BRK and RESET handler, but the game never calls it (not the game's)

hi-res page 1, the screen, drawn on every other frame. As loaded it holds the loading screen, the same picture as page 2: the counters' bar, the title lettering over the stars and the planet, and the ground. The attract mode blackens the sky before its first frame, a game redraws the bar, and the scenery and every object are drawn each frame; the ground band stays as loaded, patched by erase boxes of the same colour (runtime: the screen)
hi-res page 2, the other screen, drawn on in turn with page 1. As loaded it holds the same loading screen, byte for byte (runtime: the screen)

the language card's RAM, which the game never switches in. The loader reads $C083 twice at $03A3, which switches the card in to be read and written; as the hand-over leaves it, $E000-$FFFF holds the ROM's bytes with the RESET vector ($FFFC) pointing at the loader's error printer, $0320, and $D000-$DFFF holds $FF (the loader's, not the game's)
